lectures.name: Abortion in Canada
lectures.title: Abortion in Canada
lectures.framing: Gestational age chooses the method, and the method chooses the risks. Everything below 12 weeks can go medical or surgical; above it the options narrow and the complication profile changes. 98% of abortions are uncomplicated.
lectures.keypoints: the 70-day / 10-week / 14-week / 25-week ladder is the spine of this lecture. Cervical shock is vasovagal at the paracervical block, not haemorrhage. Asherman syndrome risk is 8% after one curettage and up to 30% after a third within 24 hours — and trauma, not infection, is the major cause. D&E is the safest 2nd-trimester method, and the limiting factor in Canada is the shrinking number of trained practitioners.

blocks.html: Mechanism. mifepristone blocks the progesterone receptor → decidual necrosis + cervical ripening → rhythmic contractions → detachment → expulsion; contractions peak at 36-48 h. misoprostol (PGE1) works down two arms — ↓ collagen → ↑ MMPs → cervical ripening, and inhibits adenyl cyclase → ↓ cAMP → ↑ calcium → ↑ uterine tone. methotrexate blocks dihydrofolate reductase, acting on cytotrophoblast, not the embryo, and is teratogenic.

Workup skeleton

- Hx/PEx — no referral needed, most clinics self-refer · gestational age by ultrasound · medical/surgical history · Rh status · consent · counselling

- Ix — ⚠ beta hCG follow-up after medical abortion: ↓ 50% by day 3 or ↓ 80% by days 7-14 = success; a plateau = failure

- Tx of failure — > 50% abort with a second 800 mcg misoprostol; < 5% need surgical evacuation

- Follow-up — appointment within 11 days; ⭐ ovulation returns 2 weeks after a 1st-trimester abortion, so contraception starts immediately — same-day IUD, implant or DepoProvera, or tubal interruption if done under GA
Dilatation required = the number of weeks of gestation. Hegar dilators; skipping mechanical dilation ↓ discomfort and ↓ infection when cervical prep is adequate.

lectures.name: Fertilization & Infertility
lectures.title: Fertilization and Infertility
lectures.framing: Infertility is 50% female and 50% male, so both partners are investigated. The workup is six steps timed to the cycle, and each step answers one question: is the brain signalling? is the cavity and are the tubes open? did she ovulate? are the sperm adequate?
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ primary infertility means she has never been PREGNANT — not that she has no children, and a partner's children from another relationship do not change it. AMH measures reserve and does NOT predict natural fertility. Male aging ↓ volume, motility and morphology but leaves sperm concentration stable, and is NOT associated with aneuploidy — that is the maternal-age effect. Recurrent pregnancy loss is ≥ 2 losses, consecutive or not, including biochemical, and ~50% stay unexplained; the treatable one is antiphospholipid antibody syndrome (5-20%), treated with heparin + aspirin at the first positive test.

blocks.html: Ordering E2, LH and FSH together is the point. An FSH of 30 alone reads as diminished reserve — but if estradiol is also 500 she is not on day 2, and that FSH may be normal. LH is checked early because it should be low; in PCOS baseline LH can be 18, which is why ovulation strips fail in PCOS.
AMH: > 28 suggests PCOS · 15-28 normal · < 15 diminished reserve. It guides IVF dosing, not natural-fertility counselling.

Confirming ovulation: mid-luteal progesterone · urine LH — a true surge is both lines equally dark, and ovulation follows in ~36 h · ultrasound (needs daily scans) · cervical mucus, 2 consecutive clear stretchy days · basal body temperature.

Irregular cycle by time since menarche: first year — normal · after 1 year — > 90 days is abnormal · 3 years to perimenopause — < 21 days, > 35 days, or < 8 cycles a year. Primary amenorrhea: no menarche by 15, or > 3 years after thelarche.

Male factors, in order: idiopathic (commonest) · varicocele (2nd) · exogenous steroids · erectile/ejaculatory dysfunction · infections · genetic (Klinefelter syndrome, Y microdeletions) · radiation/chemo · lifestyle — marijuana, smoking, hot tubs.

lectures.name: Contraception
lectures.title: Contraception and drugs used in gynecology
lectures.framing: Two questions, in this order. First, which axis is this drug on — estrogen, progestin, or androgen — because the indication and the adverse effects both follow from it. Then, for contraception specifically, counsel from the TYPICAL-use column, never the perfect-use one. Failure rates below are pregnancies per 1000 women per year of typical use.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ The progestin-only contraceptive's primary mechanism is LOCAL, not central — cervical mucus, tubal peristalsis and endometrium, with ovulation suppressed in only ~50% of cycles (the injection excepted), which is exactly why the mini-pill fails at 3 hours late while a combined pill forgives. Estrogen and progestin oppose each other on the endometrium but are synergic on the breast — the one risk adding a progestin does not fix. Combined methods are contraindicated over age 35 at more than 15 cigarettes per day, and a past deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism contraindicates them only when she is off anticoagulation AND at higher risk of recurrence. tamoxifen is the SERM that raises endometrial cancer risk; raloxifene is not — both raise VTE. clomiphene raises gonadotropins by blocking central negative feedback, which is why an estrogen receptor antagonist induces ovulation.

lectures.name: Drugs Used in Gynecology
lectures.title: Drugs Used in Gynecology
lectures.framing: Every agent here does one of three things: disrupt the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian (HPO) axis, block the overgrowth of a sex-hormone-dependent tissue, or replace a hormone that is absent. Work out which, and the indications and adverse effects follow from it.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ The progestin-only contraceptive's primary mechanism is local, not central — that is the single most-tested fact here, and it is what makes adherence matter so much more for the mini-pill. Every contraindication in the combined column is an ESTROGEN contraindication — which is why the answer to “what can she have instead?” is almost always a progestin-only or intrauterine method. migraine with aura and an acute thromboembolic event are category ④ for combined methods only; hypertension crosses from relative to absolute at ≥ 160 systolic or ≥ 100 diastolic. The patch and the ring bypass first-pass metabolism, and that — not the dose — is why they carry more VTE risk than the pill. Drospirenone is the anti-androgenic progestin (spironolactone-derived) — the one to reach for in hormonal acne, and the one that risks hyperkalemia; estranes and gonanes are androgenic instead. Ulipristal beats levonorgestrel at every interval, including inside 72 hours ⚠ — an Elentra module question keys this the other way, and the lecture's own meta-analysis slide is the one to trust. GnRH agonists flare before they suppress; antagonists never flare. Finasteride lowers DHT, it does not block the androgen receptor — which is why it shrinks a prostate and thins body hair without touching muscle mass. ⚠ No emergency contraceptive works once implantation has happened — only mifepristone acts on an established pregnancy.

lectures.name: Vaginal Discharge
lectures.title: Vaginal Discharge
lectures.framing: pH is the first discriminator and it splits the four diagnoses in half. estrogen drives discharge containing glycogen, which feeds lactobacilli and holds the pH acidic — so a pH above 4.5 means the flora has already changed.
lectures.keypoints: Know the ranking, the symptoms and the diagnostic test; for treatment know the route, not the dose. BV is the #1 infectious vaginitis and is NOT an STI — but it potentiates acquiring one, which is half the reason to treat it. A symptomatic swab reporting "altered vaginal flora" is treated as BV. The classic trichomonas findings are the rare ones — frothy discharge in < 10%, strawberry cervix in only 2%, and the exam may be entirely normal. Trichomonas coexists with BV in 60%; 20% of women culture positive for Candida while asymptomatic, which is why it is treated only when symptomatic. Physiologic discharge is stretchy like raw egg white at ovulation — ↑ estrogen, not disease.

Shared downstream risk: post-operative cuff infection after hysterectomy follows both BV and trichomoniasis — the anaerobic environment is what the two have in common.

Workup skeleton

- Hx — amount, colour, odour vs odourless, onset, better/worse, past treatments, itch or rash, full gyn and sexual history

- PEx — ⭐ look at the vulva and vagina, not just the cervix — they have their own pathology · hair pattern and removal (folliculitis) · architecture · speculum

- Ix — swab the lateral walls, away from the cervix · pH strips read 3.5-7 and are read while still WET (blood has a pH of 7) · whiff test: 10% KOH alkalizes the amines anaerobes make · wet mount, saline or KOH, read on low and high power

lectures.title: Cervical Cancer Screening
lectures.framing: Screening works because the precursor lasts years. Most HPV infections clear; some produce a squamous intraepithelial lesion; a few progress to carcinoma, usually after 10+ years. Treat the lesion and the cancer never happens — which is why cervical cancer is 16th in Canada and 4th worldwide.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ eligibility is any ASYMPTOMATIC person with a cervix who has EVER been sexually active, from about age 25 — screening is not for symptomatic people, and a never-sexually-active patient may defer. Vaccination does not replace screening. At least 75% of people are exposed to HPV in a lifetime and condoms are only partially protective, because transmission is skin-to-skin beyond what a condom covers. In Ontario NIPT-style logic does not apply here: primary HPV screening is the direction of travel, but the sample must still include the transformation zone. ⚠ An LSIL alone does not tell you which strain caused it — which is why the strain matters more than the grade.

England has almost eliminated cervical cancer in women born since 1 September 1995, most in those vaccinated at 12-13.

Sample collection — what gets a specimen rejected: know the system — ThinPrep: do NOT leave the device in the vial; SurePath: it may be left · lukewarm water for the speculum, and gel only if water-based and sparing · full legal name, DOB, collection date · check the vial expiry.

Self-sampling. She collects her own vaginal sample; it holds mostly vaginal cells and only rare cervical cells, and HPV testing still works purely because the test is that sensitive. It exists to reach the under- and never-screened. Australia offers it to all screen-eligible people since 2022; British Columbia to specific populations. Equivalence to provider sampling is cautious optimism, not settled.

lectures.framing: This lecture is about the population, not the patient. The clinical question is who has an infection; the public-health question is what makes a disease reportable, and what does reporting buy.
lectures.keypoints: the list of risk factors is broad enough that most sexually active people meet at least one — which is the argument for offering testing rather than selecting for it. ⭐ Reportability is what makes contact tracing possible, so it is not an administrative detail but the mechanism by which a diagnosed infection stops spreading. 48% of abortions worldwide are unsafe and 97% of those are in developing countries — the same inequity shapes the STI burden.

blocks.html: Reportable STBBIs: chlamydia · gonorrhea · HIV · syphilis · hepatitis B · hepatitis C.
Locally: chlamydia is the commonest STI in London; gonorrhea and syphilis are rising; HIV rates have been stable.

Gonococcal resistance has forced three changes of drug class: penicillins and tetracyclines until resistance emerged in the 1980s → fluoroquinolones in the 1990s → 3rd generation cephalosporins since the mid-2000s.

Risk factors, grouped by what they actually describe

- Partner — sexual contact with a known STI · a new partner, or more than two in the past year · a serially monogamous pattern, since these individuals are less likely to be tested · anonymous partnering (internet, bathhouse, rave)

- Age — ⭐ sexually active youth under 25, in whom chlamydia and gonorrhea are especially concentrated

- Contraception — none, or sole use of a non-barrier method: oral contraceptives, Depo Provera and the IUD all count, because none is a barrier

- Substances — injection drug use · alcohol, cannabis, cocaine, ecstasy, crystal meth, especially when associated with sex

- Practices — unprotected oral, genital or anal sex · sex with blood exchange, including sadomasochism · sharing sex toys

- Circumstance — sex workers and clients · "survival sex", exchanging sex for money, drugs, shelter or food · street involvement and homelessness · victims of sexual assault or abuse

- History — a previous STI

lectures.framing: Two questions run this lecture: is the pregnancy inside the uterus, and is it viable? A positive beta hCG with pain or bleeding is an ectopic pregnancy until the ultrasound says otherwise, and the ultrasound is only interpretable against the β-hCG level.
lectures.keypoints: β-hCG is the most important predictor of methotrexate failure — 92% success below 5000, and 4x the failure rate above it. Half of miscarriages have a normal karyotype; of the abnormal half, trisomy 16 is commonest and always lethal, and XO is the commonest isolated aneuploidy. Cerclage is elective at 12-16 weeks and rescue below 23 weeks.

blocks.html: Ectopic pregnancy. Sites: tube 80% — ampulla 70%, isthmus 12%, fimbria 6% — interstitial 2%, ovarian 0.5-3%, cervical < 0.1%, abdominal and C/S scar 1 in 2000, heterotopic 1 in 30,000 but 1% with ART. ⚠ This deck says 2% of pregnancies and 80% tubal; the acute pelvic pain deck says 6-16% and 98% tubal.

Workup skeleton

- Hx/PEx — the triad is abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding and a positive β-hCG; then displaced or enlarged uterus, orthostatic hypotension, pelvic mass, bulging fornix, cervical motion tenderness, shoulder pain from diaphragmatic irritation

- Ix — β-hCG doubles every 1.4-2.1 days, and 85% of viable IUPs rise ≥ 66% in 48 h · CBC, group and screen · TVUS should see an IUP above a β-hCG of 1500, and 99% by 3150 (transabdominal needs 6500) · "ring of fire" · free fluid

- Tx — expectant if β-hCG declining and < 200, mass < 3.5 cm, no rupture, asymptomatic · methotrexate 50 mg/m² IM ⚠ not mg/kg · surgery for instability, rupture, MTX contraindication

- ⭐ Any Rh-negative patient with a positive β-hCG and vaginal bleeding needs Rh immunoglobulin — WinRho or Rhogam — to protect her future pregnancies

lectures.title: Endometriosis
lectures.framing: Endometrial tissue outside the uterine cavity, and the disease does not behave the way its extent predicts. ⭐ The severity of disease does not correlate with the degree of pain, and the examination is often normal — which is why it takes years to diagnose.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ most women with endometriosis do NOT experience infertility, despite it being the headline complication. Pain begins about 2 days BEFORE menses — which is what separates it from primary dysmenorrhea, where pain comes with the bleeding. Many patients have had YEARS without a diagnosis, told repeatedly that painful periods are normal in the teenage years.

blocks.html: Two ways to suppress ovulation, and the split is the discriminator. Pseudopregnancy — flood it with progestin: OCP, NuvaRing, Evra patch, Depo Provera, hormonal IUS, Visanne. Pseudomenopause — withdraw the estrogen: danazol, a testosterone derivative, and Lupron or Zoladex, GnRH agonists.

Why it causes infertility — four separate mechanisms: embryotoxic factors in the peritoneal fluid · lower implantation rates · impaired follicle development with diminished reserve · impaired tubal transport from a chronically pro-inflammatory pelvis.

Diagnosis. Gold standard is laparoscopy with biopsy, and the pathologist needs ⭐ any 2 of 3: endometrial glands or epithelium, endometrial stroma, and hemosiderin. Early lesions are "blueberry"; late ones are "powder burns" with adhesions, and ⚠ late disease burns out — no endometrial tissue remains, so a negative late biopsy does not exclude it. Because not everyone can be scoped, most diagnoses rest on symptoms and response to medical therapy.

Staging uses the revised ASRM classification — I-II minimal/mild, superficial plaques without significant adhesions; III-IV moderate/severe, ovarian involvement, deep disease, dense adhesions, kissing ovaries, a frozen pelvis.

Dyspareunia — ask, because she will not raise it. "Have you ever had penetrative sexual activity? If yes, do you experience pain with it?" Maintain a non-judgmental, normalizing approach. Superficial pain on penetration points to vulvodynia, atrophy, vulvar skin conditions or vaginismus; deep pain points to endometriosis, masses, adhesions or musculoskeletal causes.

A ruptured cyst mimics a ruptured ectopic exactly, and only the β-hCG separates them. Significant haemorrhage from a ruptured cyst is uncommon — most bleed minimally, which is why instability is notable.

Workup skeleton

- Hx — onset · duration · quality · location · radiation · aggravating and relieving factors · associated GI, GU, fever, discharge, bleeding · past medical, surgical, medication, gynecologic and family history · ⭐ the social history matters enormously in pelvic pain

- PEx — vitals · general appearance · abdomen (inspection, auscultation, palpation) · pelvic (inspection, palpation)

- Ix — CBC · ⭐ quantitative beta hCG · urinalysis and culture · vaginal and cervical cultures · ultrasound · group and screen

Which ovaries tort: a normal ovary can, but rarely. Enlarged ovaries behave like a weighted pendulum — so torsion is usually a symptom of an underlying mass, benign or malignant.

Differential by system: gynecologic — pregnancy and its complications, dysmenorrhea, endometritis, neoplasm, salpingitis · GI — appendicitis, obstruction, diverticulitis, intussusception, Crohn's disease · urologic — cystitis, pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis · MSK — hernia, trauma, muscle strain · vascular — ischaemic bowel, sickle crisis · neurologic — herpes zoster, abdominal migraine · respiratory — pneumonia.

lectures.framing: Pain below the umbilicus for at least 6 months, severe enough to cause functional disability or require treatment. ⭐ Acute pain is protective; chronic pain serves no physiologic purpose, and the intensity is often not proportional to the tissue damage — which is why the examination so often finds less than the story predicts.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ up to 50% of women with chronic pelvic pain have experienced some kind of abuse or trauma — take the history. Boggy distinguishes adenomyosis from the firm irregular uterus of fibroids. Pain with no cyclic pattern and a normal structural examination is myofascial, and the honest goal there is pain reduction and improved function, not cure.

blocks.html: Why NSAIDs are first line in dysmenorrhea. Menses is a generalized inflammatory state: prostaglandins from endometrial sloughing induce contractions → uterine pressure exceeds arterial pressure → uterine ischaemia → anaerobic metabolites accumulate → stimulate type C pain neurons. Any hormonal method that reduces menstrual flow improves it, because there is less endometrium to slough.

Fibroids — location decides everything. More common in African American, obese, early menarche and hereditary cases; ⭐ smoking is associated with LESS risk. Submucosal → bleeding and hysteroscopic resection · intramural and subserosal → uterine artery embolization · pedunculated → risk of torsion, and myomectomy or hysterectomy. Reproductive dysfunction only occurs with fibroids that distort the cavity. ⚠ Pregnancy after uterine artery embolization is NOT advised — case reports only, which is what separates UAE from myomectomy for a patient who still wants to conceive.

Where the pain can come from: pelvic viscera (uterus, ovaries, bladder, urethra, rectum, sigmoid) · somatic structures (skin, vulva, clitoris, vagina) · MSK and ligamentous structures · GI and urologic referred pain. Chronic pelvic pain accounts for 10% of outpatient gynecology referrals, 40% of laparoscopies and 20% of hysterectomies for benign disease.

A mass at the os narrows the differential to the structural letters and away from the functional ones, which is the entire method of this lecture.

Why adenomyosis produces those two symptoms: more endometrial tissue, plus entrapped blood in cystic areas that rupture → bleeding; the myometrium contracting because blood irritates it, plus the same rupture → pain.

LP is the only lichen in the vagina and mouth — so a normal vulva does not end the examination.

blocks.html: Vulvar masses. Bartholin's gland cysts and abscesses are the commonest disorder of the gland; carcinoma is rare. Cysts are usually asymptomatic; abscesses are tender, warm, soft or fluctuant, with difficulty walking or sitting — ⚠ location is key, do not confuse it with a labial abscess. Treat with incision and drainage, a Word catheter, or marsupialization. A vulvar lipoma is soft and painless, 1 cm to > 10 cm, and the patient often has lipomas elsewhere.

Aphthae — after a viral syndrome, in girls 9-20, treated with prednisone. Vitiligo — screen for autoimmune disease (TSH, anti-TPO, anti-thyroglobulin, fasting glucose). Molluscum contagiosum — a poxvirus, umbilicated papules, never on palms and soles, self-limiting. Yeast vulvitis — splash dysuria, satellite lesions, fissures.

- Hx/PEx — ⭐ LOOK and FEEL: cancers feel firm and can be tender, and the inguinal node chain must be palpated

- Most VIN is multifocal and sits on the NON-hairy vulva; lesions are often raised, verrucous and white, but may be red, pink, gray or brown

- ⚠ LS, LP, condylomata acuminata and condyloma lata all mimic VIN — if one is suspected and the lesion does not fully resolve or is refractory to therapy, biopsy it

- Ix — ⭐ when in doubt = BIOPSY; multiple biopsies if areas differ; at minimum a 4 mm punch

lectures.keypoints: ⭐ the vFib arrest with a haemoglobin of 38 was diagnosed because someone finally asked about her cycles — previously 28-day cycles with a pad every 4 hours, now 14-45 day cycles with a pad more than hourly, flooding and clots. Nobody had asked. DUB cannot be reached while a structural cause is unexplained, because it is a diagnosis of exclusion. Every patient over 40 with AUB gets an endometrial biopsy.

blocks.html: Physical exam is where the functional causes show themselves. lectures.name: Genetic Screening for Pregnancy in Canada
lectures.title: Genetic Screening for Pregnancy in Canada
lectures.framing: Primary prevention happens before conception; secondary prevention happens after it. ⭐ Every couple has a 2-3% chance of a baby with some congenital anomaly regardless of screening — that baseline never reaches zero, and every result is interpreted against it.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ in Ontario NIPT is NOT recommended as a first-line screen for low-risk women, despite being the best performer in the table — which is why the funded indications (previous trisomy, maternal age 40+, NT > 3.5 mm, positive eFTS) exist. A positive screen always needs a diagnostic test. Cytology of the family matters: when a fetal aneuploidy proves translocation-derived, karyotype the parents — a daughter has a 50% chance of carrying it and the carrier's siblings need counselling too.

lectures.title: Approach to Amenorrhea
lectures.framing: Amenorrhea is a compartment problem — the block sits in the outflow tract, the ovary, the pituitary or the hypothalamus — and two numbers sort it: the beta hCG first, always, then FSH, which says whether the pituitary is shouting at a dead ovary (high FSH) or not shouting at all (low FSH).
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ rule out pregnancy first, before any other test and whatever the story sounds like. High FSH means the ovary has failed; low FSH means the problem is above it — that one number splits the differential, and a normal FSH with normal prolactin and TSH points at anovulation, which is where PCOS lives. PCOS is the commonest secondary cause (28%), Turner the commonest primary (27%). ⚠ The workbook keys primary amenorrhea as "no periods by 16"; the lecture uses 13 without and 15 with secondary sex characteristics — answer to the source in front of you.

lectures.name: Hysterectomy Approaches
lectures.title: Hysterectomy approaches
lectures.framing: Choose the least invasive route the anatomy allows. Every approach is a "short stay" with same-day discharge except abdominal, and the whole lecture is a ladder: vaginal → LAVH → TLH or robotic → abdominal, where each rung is what to use when the one above is blocked. ⚠ When the indication is bleeding control, medical options come first - hysterectomy is for failed medical management and special circumstances.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Abdominal is the only approach not planned as same-day discharge - it needs a 2-3 day hospital stay. Vaginal is the only approach without abdominal entry, and the one that cannot get at tubes and ovaries. Shared limitation of every minimally invasive route is a large uterus; the vaginal-route pair add narrow introitus/pelvis and poor uterine descent, and the laparoscopic pair add suturing skill and operative time. TLH and robotic replace abdominal, not vaginal/LAVH.

lectures.name: Dilation and Curettage
lectures.title: Dilation and curettage
lectures.framing: One procedure, one objective: know what goes wrong and what you do about it. A D&C is vacuum aspiration of a pregnancy under 14 weeks through a rigid cannula on electric suction; every complication is a consequence of one step, so learn the complications by the step that causes them.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Antibiotic prophylaxis is indicated for therapeutic abortion but NOT for a D&C done for missed abortion or pregnancy loss - the same procedure, two indications, one gets antibiotics. ⚠ Asherman's follows curettage in 8%, and repeat curettage (for retained products or retained placenta post partum) raises it to 30% by a third consecutive procedure - which is why retained products are managed with misoprostol where possible rather than a reflex second D&C. Hematometra is re-evacuated immediately; retained products may wait for medical management - the two "something is still in the uterus" complications get opposite tempos.

lectures.name: Clinical Approach to Menopause
lectures.title: Clinical approach to menopause
lectures.framing: Every treatment decision splits on which symptom you are treating: vasomotor symptoms are systemic and need systemic therapy; GSM is local and is treated locally. Estrogen is the gold standard for VMS and the second line for GSM, so the real question is whether she can have it systemically: no contraindications, younger than 60, and < 10 years post menopause.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Estrogen is the gold standard for VMS, and a woman with a uterus must have progesterone with it; estrogen alone only after hysterectomy. Vaginal estrogen treats GSM but not VMS, and systemic MHT can under-treat GSM, so some women need both. Transdermal estrogen skips first-pass metabolism and has the better clotting profile. After menopause estradiol and progesterone fall while FSH and LH rise (loss of feedback). A history of VTE or stroke is enough to contraindicate estrogen - it need not be active.

lectures.name: Approach to and Pathology of a Pelvic Mass
lectures.title: Ovarian neoplasms
lectures.framing: Every ovarian tumour is named by its lineage (epithelial, germ cell, sex cord/stromal) plus its behaviour (benign, borderline, malignant), and the age of the patient predicts the lineage: epithelial in adults, germ cell in the young. Most ovarian neoplasms are not malignant; cancer is more likely post-menopausal.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Beware the bilateral atypical mucinous tumour: it is a metastasis until the appendix has been checked, and the classic metastatic pattern is bilateral and multi-nodular. Serous carcinoma is the #1 ovarian cancer and presents late, which is why mortality is high. Borderline vs carcinoma = invasion, not architecture. Mucinous carcinoma is the one carcinoma that is usually unilateral. Granulosa cell tumour recurs late (> 10 yr) and ruptures; its estrogen shows up in the endometrium first.

lectures.framing: Any bleeding after 12 months without menses is PMB, and the whole approach turns on one rule: endometrial carcinoma must be excluded in every woman with PMB, however benign the story. The most common cause is atrophy; the most serious is carcinoma or hyperplasia. The investigation is the same for both: speculum exam, TVUS, and endometrial biopsy.

Risk factors for hyperplasia and type 1 carcinoma are the same: unopposed estrogen. ⚠ Insufficient endometrial tissue is not a benign result - repeat the sampling. Endometrial cancer is the #1 gyn malignancy and the 4th most common cancer in women; endometrial names the site, endometrioid names the (most common) type.

lectures.title: Pathology of the breast
lectures.framing: Place the lesion by the tissue it arises from, then tell the lesions of that tissue apart by presentation. The TDLU grows fibrocystic change and carcinoma (in situ and invasive); the large ducts and nipple grow papillomas, duct ectasia, mastitis and Paget's; the intralobular stroma grows fibroadenoma and phyllodes; the interlobular stroma and fat grow fat necrosis, PASH and mesenchymal tumours.

lectures.name: OB Care Providers
lectures.title: Obstetrical care providers
lectures.framing: Three providers, one team. The chart turns on who can do what, and at which point a pregnancy leaves their scope: family medicine and midwives each carry a low-risk pregnancy from antenatal care to 6 weeks post partum, while the obstetrician is the consultant for anything complicated and the only one who operates.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Midwives provide informed choice rather than informed consent, which is why a client can choose outside the regular recommendations. ⚠ The obstetrician provides no care for the infant and has no lactation training; the family physician follows the baby from birth onward and the midwife for 6 weeks. Fetal anomalies at any stage go to MFM, not a general OB. Preeclampsia is a consult trigger in all three phases, and the post partum list is short: PPH, a 3rd or 4th degree tear, preeclampsia. Asking for help is not a failure.

lectures.name: Pathology of 1st Trimester Bleeding

lectures.framing: Three "baby" causes of first trimester bleeding, told apart by where the products of conception are and what the trophoblast is doing. lectures.name: Teratogenesis
lectures.title: Teratogenesis
lectures.framing: A teratogen is judged by what it hits and when: the same exposure does nothing in weeks 1-2, produces a major structural anomaly during organogenesis (weeks 3-8), and a functional or minor defect in the fetal period. 9 in 10 pregnant women take at least one medication, so the question is rarely whether she is exposed but how to counsel her.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Weeks 3-8 (organogenesis) is the window of greatest sensitivity; weeks 1-2 are usually not susceptible, and the fetal period is less sensitive - CNS, eyes and external genitalia stay sensitive to term. ⚠ FDA category C means no data, not safety; the D/X split is benefit may outweigh risk vs. risk outweighs any benefit. Hyperthermia and maternal diabetes both cause NTDs and cardiovascular defects - hyperthermia adds abdominal wall defects and spontaneous abortion, diabetes adds CNS, spine and limb defects.

lectures.framing: Two questions, one for each half of the lecture. For dating: which landmark is visible decides which measurement dates the pregnancy, and each landmark is retired the moment the next one appears. For a positive test with an empty uterus: a single hCG value never settles a pregnancy of unknown location; only the rate of change does, so the answer is almost always to repeat it.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Once an embryo is seen, MSD is never used again: CRL dates the pregnancy, best when > 10 mm (7 weeks), accurate to 3-8 days. A gestational sac is visible from 32 days, a yolk sac from 5 to 5+5 weeks, a heartbeat by 6+0. hCG level does not predict ectopic rupture, and a falling hCG does not exclude an ectopic: 8% of untreated ectopics fall at the same rate as a miscarriage (Silva 2006). All women should be offered a dating scan at 7-12 weeks; it beats LMP and cuts inductions for post-dates.

lectures.framing: Every decision turns on two questions: when did the BP rise relative to 20 weeks, and is the high BP the disease itself (chronic / gestational) or a symptom of it (pre-eclampsia / eclampsia)? Mild is >140 / >90, severe is >160 / >110, always 2 readings >15 min apart. ⚠ HELLP can present with a completely normal BP. The primary maternal danger of severe HTN is stroke, so any neurological symptom means investigate for an intracranial event. Treat the number in chronic / gestational HTN; in pre-eclampsia the number is a symptom and complications drive delivery planning.

lectures.name: Topics of Antenatal Care
lectures.title: Topics in antenatal care
lectures.framing: Three routine pieces of antenatal care, each with a when and a why: feed the pregnancy (folate + iron), vaccinate it (inactivated only), and screen the mother's blood. The antibody question turns on one thing: does she already have an antibody? If not, RhIG prevents one; if so, the titre decides whether the fetus is watched.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ The only vaccine category not considered safe is live attenuated (MMR, varicella, BCG), and the reason is a theoretical one, not an observed one. Tdap is timed (27-32 wk) because the point is the baby's passive immunity; influenza is not timed because the point is the mother. RhIG is prophylaxis for the unsensitized: it clears fetal cells before the maternal immune system responds, so it does nothing once an antibody exists. ⚠ A titre of 1/8 or greater is the line for severe-anemia risk; below it, keep testing monthly. Sensitization needs a source: previous pregnancy, transfusion, or drug abuse (module Q94), and the fetus is only at risk if it carries the antigen, hence the partner screen.

lectures.framing: Three jobs in the first 12 weeks: confirm the pregnancy, date it, and screen it. Every question turns on a threshold or a counting rule, and the one rule above the rest: once the EDB is set by the most reliable method (IVF transfer date, or 1st-trimester ultrasound) it is FIXED - a later scan that disagrees is reporting growth, not a new due date.

A gestational sac alone does not confirm a pregnancy - the yolk sac is required, and location must be established to exclude ectopic. CRL after 14 weeks is not a dating tool. lectures.name: Approach to Sexual Health
lectures.title: Approach to sexual health
lectures.framing: Two halves to this lecture: the physiology you contrast between cis-men and cis-women, and the interview you run so the patient can raise the problem they came in with. The whole conversation turns on one move: acknowledge your own implicit biases before you walk into the room, then ask permission to talk about sexual health, so the patient never has to raise it first.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ The refractory period is the sex difference: males are physiologically incapable of another orgasm after the first; females have none and can have multiple orgasms. NO is the neurotransmitter of clitoral engorgement, and photoplethysmography is how VBV is measured. Orgasm is cerebral, not spinal. The interview separates on repetition as the tool that unpacks a euphemism, and on asking permission first. ⚠ Never assume orientation or monogamy in the wording: "How many partners in the past year?", not "Are you monogamous?"; say "partner".

lectures.name: Antepartum Hemorrhage & Abnormal Placentation
lectures.title: Antepartum hemorrhage
lectures.framing: Bleeding in the 2nd/3rd trimester turns on two questions: is it painful, and whose blood is it? A painful bleed with a tender uterus is an abruption, a painless bleed is a previa until the ultrasound says otherwise, and a small bleed with a distressed fetus is fetal blood - a vasa previa. Whatever the cause, assess mother and fetus together, continuously, and remember that ongoing bleeding depletes clotting factors at the placental interface.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Painful bleeding + tender uterus = abruption; painless bleeding = previa; small bleed + fetal distress = vasa previa, and the blood is fetal. ⚠ Never examine the cervix of a bleeder until ultrasound has cleared the placenta. Kleihaur-Betke finds fetal blood in the mother; Apt finds it in the vaginal blood - only Apt diagnoses vasa previa. Abruption is a diagnosis of exclusion; previa is an ultrasound diagnosis. A previous C/S raises the risk of previa and accreta, not vasa previa; vasa previa comes from a velamentous cord (type 1) or a succenturiate lobe (type 2).

blocks.lead:
Workup skeleton

- Hx: previous bleeding this pregnancy · previous abruption · trauma (MVC, fall) · hypertension, autoimmune disease · smoking/cocaine · previous C/S or uterine surgery (accreta) · placental location on the anatomy scan

- PEx: maternal vitals · abdominal exam for uterine tenderness/rigidity and fetal presentation · speculum for the source · ⚠ no cervical examination until ultrasound has shown the placenta is clear of the cervix - examining a previa can precipitate massive hemorrhage

- Ix: stat CBC (baseline Hb, platelets) · INR/PTT/fibrinogen (coagulopathy) · creatinine · ± LFTs (r/o pre-eclampsia, acute liver injury) · group and screen · Kleihaur-Betke test = fetal blood in the maternal circulation (trauma, abruption) · Apt test = fetal blood in the vaginal bleed (vasa previa) · ultrasound for placental location

- Tx: active bleed + preterm: birthing unit, continuous fetal monitoring, steroids for lungs, MgSO4 for neuroprotection, NICU/tertiary consult if <28-32 weeks, serial bloods q4-6 h · term or late preterm (>35-36 weeks): deliver - induction if reassuring, C/S if not

- Follow-up: preterm, stable and bleeding settled: antenatal ward, NST + growth/placental-function ultrasound, periodic bloods by initial values and rebleeding

How hemorrhage becomes coagulopathy: the high-volume flow to the placental-uterine interface and the inability to acutely clot over large exposed vessels means platelets and clotting factors are quickly consumed - a consumptive coagulopathy, which is why fibrinogen is on the stat bloodwork.

lectures.name: Approach to the Small Fetus
lectures.title: Approach to the small fetus
lectures.framing: Three labels that sound alike and mean different things: SGA is a percentile, LBW is a weight, IUGR is a pathological process, and the first two say nothing about the third. The job is to find the fetus that is IUGR as early as possible, name the cause, then let the Doppler and the gestational age decide delivery.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ SGA is a percentile (<10th), LBW is a weight (<2500 g), IUGR is a process, and an IUGR fetus can be above the 10th percentile. SFH >2-3 cm less than weeks screens; ultrasound EFW confirms. A trisomy is the intrinsic cause; smoking, hypertension and multiples restrict nutrient delivery. Placental insufficiency below the 3rd percentile shows absent EDF and ↓ amniotic fluid, not polyhydramnios. Delivery, not time, is the only way to feed the fetus better.

- Tx: reverse the reversible (smoking, hypertension) to limit worsening · ⚠ no catch-up growth in utero; delivery is the only true way to improve nutrient delivery · if premature: steroids for lung maturation, transfer to NICU-level care

- Follow-up: frequency set by severity and by NST / Doppler findings

lectures.name: Approach to Preterm Labour
lectures.title: Approach to preterm labour
lectures.framing: Everything turns on where she sits on one line: threatened preterm labour → preterm labour → preterm birth, with membranes intact or ruptured. Each step adds the intervention that buys the next one time: hydrate, then tocolyse to buy 48 hours, spend them on steroids and transfer, and when birth is imminent switch to magnesium and penicillin.
lectures.keypoints: ⚠ Antibiotics in PPROM INCREASE latency (the inherited note had it backwards). Steroids are the one intervention given at every stage; tocolysis needs contractions, magnesium needs an imminent birth, penicillin needs a delivery. Cerclage is for cervical insufficiency before 24 weeks, never for ruptured membranes. Dehydration and UTI mimic TPTL: hydrate and dip the urine before reaching for a tocolytic.

- Ix: nitrazine + ferning, ultrasound for low amniotic fluid · urinalysis (UTI mimics TPTL) · GBS swab if not done · ⚠ amniocentesis for bacteria is NOT a validated test for rupture of membranes

lectures.name: Process of Labour and Birth
lectures.title: Process of labour and birth
lectures.framing: Labour is regular uterine contractions causing progressive cervical dilation, and each stage asks the same two questions: what event ends it, and what am I measuring to know it is progressing. The 1st stage is measured on the cervix, the 2nd on the fetus, the 3rd on the placenta, the 4th on the mother.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ true labour = regular contractions causing progressive cervical dilation; Braxton Hicks change nothing at the cervix. Station is measured from the ischial spines, dilation is complete at 10 cm. ⚠ The earliest sign of placental separation is the firm, globular uterus, not the gush of blood. ⚠ In the 4th stage the danger is PPH on top of a 500 mL autotransfusion, so a cardiac patient needs watching for the ↑ cardiac work.

lectures.name: Abnormal Labour
lectures.title: Abnormal labour and birth
lectures.framing: Every route in this lecture gets a baby out when labour will not do it alone, and each one has a gate. The Bishop score gates induction, a fully dilated cervix with an engaged vertex gates an instrument, a low segment scar gates TOLAC, and in a PPH a firm or an atonic uterus decides the next step.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Uterine atony is the primary cause of PPH, and the rate is rising - so a firm uterus sends you looking for trauma instead. Abnormal FHR is the #1 reason for an operative vaginal delivery and the first sign of a uterine rupture. ⚠ Vacuum cannot rotate; forceps can. A previous C/S for dystocia lowers VBAC success; a non-recurrent indication (breech) raises it. ⚠ Carboprost in asthma, ergonovine in hypertension.

lectures.name: Hemorrhagic Shock
lectures.title: Hemorrhagic shock
lectures.framing: Shock is cellular hypoxia, and hemorrhagic shock is the hypovolemic kind: lost blood → ↓ preload → ↓ cardiac output. The whole lecture turns on one thing: grade the loss from the vitals, then resuscitate before the vitals agree with you, because the obstetric patient is young, healthy and volume-expanded, so she compensates until she suddenly does not.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Blood pressure is normal through class II (up to 30% loss, ~1500 mL); it falls only in class III, so a normal BP does not exclude shock and tachycardia (> 100, class II) is the first vital to move. ⚠ Do not overlook the young healthy patient: she may surprise you with how much she has lost while still looking well. Bleeding is treated by stopping the bleeding; fluids and blood buy time, and each unit given feeds the coagulopathy arm of the triad.

blocks.lead:
Workup skeleton

- Hx / recognise: the 8 features of shock: hypotension · tachycardia · oliguria · abnormal mental status · tachypnea · cool, clammy, cyanotic skin · metabolic acidosis · hyperlactatemia

- First moves: ABCs and call for HELP · vitals (HR, BP, RR, O2 sat) with ABG / VBG · large-bore IV x 2, crystalloids / colloids · O2 · Foley to urometer (urine output is a vital sign here)

- Ix: CBC · G+S · PTT/INR · fibrinogen · Cr

- Tx: blood products (pRBC, platelets, cryo, FFP) → ? massive transfusion protocol · identify and address the cause, stop the bleeding · ? ICU (inotropes, central lines)

- Throughout: prevent the lethal triad (below)

blocks.html: Why OBGYN is different: the population is young and healthy, and the post-partum woman has a pregnancy-expanded blood volume built for the blood loss of delivery, so she compensates well despite a large loss.

lectures.name: Lactation
lectures.title: Lactation
lectures.framing: Lactation needs three things: prolactin to make milk, oxytocin to eject it, and removal of milk by infant or pump, which must begin by day 3. Nearly every breastfeeding problem is a failure of one of the three, so ask which one broke.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ By day 3 control switches from endocrine to autocrine: milk removal, not hormone, now drives supply, which is why removal must start by day 3 and why poor extraction lowers production. Low supply is the most common reason to stop breastfeeding. Mastitis is treated by continuing to nurse, not by stopping; an abscess needs drainage. Breast size doesn't matter. Alcohol is not a contraindication; smoking and street drugs are to be avoided.

blocks.html: Contraindications: HIV in developed countries (WHO: OK if both on ART) · active psychosis · active TB · herpetic breast lesions · antineoplastic drugs · infant galactosemia · PKU with high infant phenylalanine · patient refuses.
Contraception: ⚠ avoid estrogen-containing products - ↓ quality and quantity of milk. Safe: hormonal or copper IUD · progesterone-only pill · barrier · Depo-Provera.
Formula supplementation: patient choice · inadequate supply with poor growth / failure to thrive · infant dehydration, hypoglycemia, weight loss or poor gain.

Stopping: cabergoline 1 mg once · ⚠ abrupt weaning not recommended - rapid ↓ prolactin may ↑ depressive symptoms; gradual, child-led after 6 months is easiest · supportive bra, ice, analgesics, cabbage leaves.

Numbers: storage laws of 6 - room 6 h · fridge 6 d · freezer 6 mo · medications: milk concentration < 10% of maternal weight-adjusted dose · start within 1 hour of birth, skin to skin, feed on infant cues.

lectures.name: Postpartum Care
lectures.title: Postpartum care
lectures.framing: The puerperium is a return to baseline on a fixed timetable, so the complication is whatever breaks the timetable: blues past 2 weeks, bright red bleeding returning after 24 h, fever on 2 of the first 10 days.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Blues that last more than 2 weeks, or are severe within the first 2 weeks, are postpartum depression. ⚠ EPDS item 10 scored 1-3 at any total is a self-harm risk needing immediate assessment. The puerperal-infection clock excludes the first 24 h, and delayed PPH starts after 24 h. Refer ALL antepartum and postpartum patients to pelvic floor physiotherapy.

blocks.lead:
Workup skeleton (the postnatal visit)

- Hx: review of birth (OASIS, CS) · bladder · bowel · sexual function · lochia / menses · perineum / incision · emotional wellbeing + EPDS · feeding · smoking, alcohol, substances

- PEx: weight vs pre-pregnancy · BP · affect · thyroid · breasts · abdomen · perineum · pelvic

- Ix: rubella immune? TdaP up to date? · influenza · last Pap

- Tx / counsel: contraception · pelvic floor exercises · future pregnancies, and if CS, mode of birth + spacing

- ⚠ Lactational amenorrhea is NOT contraception: ovulation can occur without menstruation

blocks.html: Discharge < 48 h: assess the 4 B's, bleeding · bowel · bladder · baby care. Contraindications: preeclampsia · PPH · fever · unstable medical condition.
Contraception: no estrogen-containing method before 21 days (VTE) · debated effect on breastmilk · barriers, CHC, POP, depot Provera, hormonal and copper IUDs all usable.
Perineum and bowel: clean, dry, sitz baths, pericare bottle · fibre, fluids, laxatives · no PR medications after a 3rd or 4th degree tear.

lectures.name: Approach to Neonatal Care
lectures.title: Approach to Neonatal Care
lectures.framing: Every newborn is examined within 24 h and kept pink, warm and sweet; the extra care turns on which reserve this baby lacks: heat (no shivering), glucose (glycogen lasts 8-10 h, gluconeogenesis not normal until 2-4 days), or bilirubin clearance.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Symptomatic hypoglycemia is a medical emergency: IV dextrose, not a feed (a jittery IDM who cannot latch, glucose 2.3). The GA curves run higher the more mature the baby, so the same TSB can need treatment at 35 weeks and not at 40. ⚠ Sepsis runs through all three: hypoglycemia can be a sign of it, it causes hyperbilirubinemia, and temperature instability is a jaundice risk factor, so consider it in any sick baby.

blocks.html: Bilirubin red flags: jaundice in the first 24 h is pathologic · cord bilirubin > 68 μmol/L · rise > 85 μmol/L/day · total > 340 μmol/L · direct > 30 μmol/L or > 20% of total · jaundice > 2 wk in a term infant · unwell child.

Neurotoxicity risk factors (act at a lower TSB): < 38 wk · albumin < 30 · suspected hemolysis · suspected sepsis · hemodynamic or respiratory instability. Rules of 30 (≥ 35 wk): phototherapy when within 30 μmol/L of the threshold in a baby with these risk factors; stop when > 30 below (≥ 38 wk) or > 60 below (35-37 wk).
Phototherapy works three ways: Z → E isomerization (to bile) · cyclization to lumirubin (bile, urine) · oxidation (urine).
Encephalopathy sequence: lethargy, hypotonia, poor suck → hypertonia with opisthotonos and retrocollis, high-pitched cry, fever → seizures, coma.
